Learning can be fun-at least it can if you get the right balance of educational content and pure entertainment. Our ten years' experience of  producing educational software, including the phenomenally successful Fun School range, have given us the edge. We have listened to your demand for more specific subjects such as maths, spelling and creativity, and address this with this new, specialized range of Fun School packages.
Each program has been finely tuned by teachers and educationalists to ensure it meets the requirements of the National Curriculum, but will still provide children with hours of mind-boggling fun as they discover new and fresh ways to learn. So, you can be sure that your child is achieving the right standard for his or her age, and making the most of the time spent at the keyboard. We hope you and your child enjoy using this Fun School package!

Does your child know how to use a computer keyboard? The National Curriculum contains clear guidelines on the importance of Information Technology to every child's education. You need to ensure your child meets these requirements and give them all the encouragement you can. Fun School Paint and Create has been designed to meet these needs, including introducing your child to keyboard and mouse skills, and ensuring they have the right amount of fun and enjoyment while they learn. Choose from five entertaining activities-drawing, painting, making music, creating jigsaws and greetings cards. See tangible results they can be proud of when you print out their creations. Help them exercise their creative talents in a fun and imaginative way.

418526.overview:
Fun School 2: For the Under-6s is an educational game part of the Fun School series with this version aimed at the under sixes. Parents can choose a difficulty level for each game and also enter their own words to use. There are eight activities for a child to play and these consist of:

Shape Snap: Two shapes appear and the child must say whether the shapes are the same or not.

Teddy Count: A certain amount of Teddies move about the screen and the child must say how many are on the screen.

Find the Mole: There are five mole hills and the child selects one. If the child is wrong then the computer will say if the actual number is bigger or smaller.

Write a Letter: Here the child can move the teddy about the screen and type any letter and can also type words.

Colour Train: A coloured train moves along the rails and the child has to stop it at the matching coloured station to drop off and pick up passengers. The train changes colour once it starts moving again.

Spell a Word: A picture of an object appears and the child must type in the word.

Pick a Letter: A letter is on screen and the child must move a Teddy over the alphabet and select the matching letter and move it into a box.

Teddy Bear Picnic: The child must move a teddy through a maze to reach a picnic.

418527.overview:
Fun School 2: For the Over-8s is an educational game part of the Fun School series with this version aimed at the over eights. Parents can choose a difficulty level for each game and also enter their own words to use. There are eight activities for a child to play and these consist of:

Build a Bridge: A square sits underneath a bridge and it must be filled with various shapes and placed in the correct position to hold the bridge up.

Passage of Guardians: The child controls a robot and moves him down various passages and attempt to get past the various guardians. When a guardian is touched, it reveals a word with the letters mixed up and the child has to type the correct word to move past..

Unicorn: A robot has to save an unicorn from a burning forest by moving three objects in front of it around a winding path. The robot can only carry one object at a time and certain objects cannot be left alone with each other while the robot is away..

Logic Doors: A robot needs to move around a maze of rooms with various coloured and striped doors by using the correct matching keys it finds. The robot can only carry two keys at a time so keys will need to be dropped in order to progress.

Souvenirs: The robot needs to visit a certain amount of countries in Western Europe and needs to buy a souvenir in them as proof with just £30. After choosing a country on the map, three souvenirs appear each costing a different amount in the countries currency. A exchange rate is provided for each country.

Code Boxes: A code appears on a box and you have to decipher it to guess how many objects are in the box. There are a various amount of boxes to try with the same code solution.

Mystery Machine: The robot needs to operate the machine in the correct sequence but the instructions are in various codes. Once a code is worked out for each word the child enters the letters to receive the machine operating instructions.

Escape: Completing each of the seven activities gives the child a keyword and these are needed for a robot to escape from another maze of rooms. Only certain doors can be entered and after progressing through a certain number, the computer will ask for a keyword. Give the computer all seven words and the robot has escaped.

418528.overview:
Freddy the Frog presents six games designed to help school-starting children build on their numeracy and literacy skills. The rules for each game are explained in the form of short stories. Controls primarily use the cursor keys and enter.

Freddie is building a house, but can only add a log to his work if you solve a maths question. In the library, a list of book titles must be sorted into alphabetical order.

Successfully ordering letter and number sequences on the basketball court results in shots going in. Knowing which word is the opposite of the displayed one will help Freddy's diving.

In the shop, you have to identify which coins pay for which items, and then total up a shopping load and work out which coins pay for it. There is also a simple typing test included.

418529.overview:
Fun School 4: for 7 to 11 year olds is an educational game part of the Fun School series with this version aimed at seven, eight, nine, ten, and eleven-year-olds. There are six games and activities that allow the child to help Sammy the Spy (Agent Q) find and retrieve the stolen riches of King Raram by completing six missions with varying skill levels. The six activities consist of:

Desert Dates: Sammy and his boss have found various pyramids containing gems and secret parchments hidden behind various blocks with a date written on them. The computer will ask a question and the child must select the correct block to smash.

Travels: Sammy has to travel the world in various vehicles to find a secret destination. The computer will give a Continent, Ocean, Country, City, Sea, or River, and the child must move the vehicle around the screen to get to the selected destination.

Exchange Rates: Sammy needs clothing and equipment and the only way to get these is by answering questions on exchange rates or the cheapest item.

Timetable: Sammy needs to catch and travel on a plane by going through various stages of an airport. There are various questions the child needs to answer by looking at timetables and giving the correct answer.

Proportions: To help Sammy receive and give messages to other agents, the child must look at various grids of objects and answer questions on the proportions of various selected objects.

Spy Quiz: Sammy has to get a message from his agency's house in Quizendene but he has to climb the wall to retrieve it from the roof. The security guard will ask general knowledge questions and the child needs to give the correct answer to climb up a part of the wall.

418535.overview:
An educational text adventure with still pictures from Caroline and Ian Coombe and released in 1991. Yọu̟ have been invited to go, and play with your friends, the Fraction Goblins and have spent a messy hour or two with them in their Art Room. The problem is that the young goblins were learning Borrowing, at school today and they were set some homework. So, while you were taken to the kitchen for a snack, the goblins did their homework, using the contents of your pencil case. You return, to the Art Room to find that your pencil case has been ransacked. All you have to do now is find the
contents again. 3 pens, 4 pencils, 4 crayons, a rubber, a sharpener, a ruler and the key to your bicycle padlock. Oh, by the way, if you meet any of the older goblins as you wander round the caves, they may make you answer a fractions problem before they will let you pass. If you get stuck, you can cheat a little bit. Type in the word HELP for some magical assistance. Press a key.

418537.overview:
Fun School Specials Spelling FAIR
Now the fun really begins!
The range of Fun School Specials has been developed to help children with specific areas of learning Following the success of Fun School 4 parents and teachers have been asking for software which would focus on subjects like spelling maths and creativity skills in much greater depth. The aim of the Fun School Specials is to complement children's school work. All comply fully with the National Curriculum syllabus. SPELLING FAIR helps children master basic techniques of spelling and grammar All the programs are set in a colorful, noisy fairground, incorporating the essential "fun" element that has enabled the Fun School series to achieve sales of more than 430,000 packages in the UK alone. It encourages children to discover the delights of plural similes suffixes, prefixes and homophones. Also on disc is a 300-word dictionary containing carefully selected words which frequently cause children difficulty, including some specially chosen to help dyslexic children. 
COCONUT SHY Knock down the coconuts to delete unwanted letters and form words which match the definition oven
TEST YOUR STRENGTH Use the hammer to bash the gong and learn about unusual plurals fox-foxes)
MECHANICAL GRABBER Discover suffixes and prefixes, including general word formation and inflectional endings (eg grab grabbing, not grabing)
HAUNTED HOUSE Bring fun characters to life while getting to grips with homophones like there their and caught court
WORD JUGGLE Click on letters, moving them around to make up words to the delight of the juggler on his wobbling monocycle CIRCUS WORDS: Make human cannonball come to life while using new and familiar words to complete crosswords

418538.overview:
Fun School 2: For 6-8 Year Olds is an educational game part of the Fun School series with this version aimed at the ages of six, seven and eight. Parents can choose a difficulty level for each game and also enter their own words to use. There are eight activities for a child to play and these consist of:

Number Train: A coloured train moves along the rails and the child has to stop it at the matching coloured station to drop off and pick up passengers. Once the train has stopped at the correct station, a maths problem appears and when the correct answer is typed the train moves on and changes colour.

Maths Maze: The child has to move a frog around a maze full of creatures and when the frog touches a creature a maths problem appears and the correct answer is needed to move on.

Shopping: The child has a shopping list and the child must move the frog to the correct shop from a choice of four to select the highlighted item on the list.

Treasure Hunt: Treasure is hidden on an island made up of squares and the child must type in co-ordinates to move a frog to search that square. If the treasure isn't there then the computer says how close the frog is to the actual treasure by using cold, warm and hot.

Bounce: A hand holds a ball and the child must adjust the position and angle of the hand to throw the ball and hit an apple in a room.

Animals: This is a version of hangman where a child has ten attempts to guess the letters to make up the name of an animal. If the child guesses the word correctly then a caterpillar eats an apple. Run out of attempts and the child loses apples from a bowl..

Packing: A square needs filling with a variety of shapes in the correct position to fill it. The child moves a frog to place shapes into the square.

Number Jump: A grid of various numbers are shown to the child and a frog needs to be moved across the grid from left to right. The correct number to jump on has to be part of a multiplication table shown.

418540.overview:
These six small educational games star Freddy the Frog. Each uses simple controls to ensure that children can play without difficulty from the software.

Using forward, back, left and right keys Freddy must get to various important buildings as depicted on the screen. In Adding he is presented with a network of lily pads, some of which contain numbers or mathematical symbols. Land on these in the correct order to produce a correct sum. In the Toyshop, first identify toys from their names, then choose a toy at a specified price, and then combine goods to meet a specified price limit.

Electricity allows you to learn about circuits - by working out whether an existing layout will work, and modifying it so that it will. The next game involves telling the time, so as to get the prince his key. Funtext teaches information searching using a Ceefax-type environment.

418541.overview:
Fun School 3: for the over 7s is an educational package which is part of the Fun School series. This package is aimed at the over sevens and consists of six programs with four games starring Robbie the Robot and two utilities. Each game has various skill levels and can be adjusted to suit the child's needs. The games are:

Wordsearch: On screen is a list of words and the child has to find them hidden in a grid of letters.

Planet Maths: Each maths sign (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) can be played on its own or all together as a maths problem scrolls from right to left towards a force field. Get the answer right and the problem fires a missile that destroys the force field.

Treasure: There are various pictures and on each one are directions (north, south, east and west) to the treasure, and distance in either cm or mm.

Sentences: A paragraph with spelling and grammar mistakes is seen on screen. The child must adjust the mistakes to move on to the next paragraph.

The two utilities consist of:

Robot Draw: The child can draw various shapes with a turtle on the screen. The child must click on various options to tell the turtle where to move by direction, angle and distance.

Database: This utility gives the child the chance to use a database by putting in their own information with the use of various options. A quiz on the information entered can also be played.

418544.overview:
A friendly teddy bear is on hand to help teach the skills children should have on starting school. They are controlled using the space and return keys, so young children should be able to play with little support. Most games have multiple difficulty levels, which reveal themselves after the easiest has been solved.

If Teddy's friend is to climb the tree successfully, you must recognise which of the items in front of you can be paired up. Initially there are 6, rising to 18 as you get them right. The Gallery game involves matching pictures with the correct label, with more and more options as the game difficulty increases. In the actions game you must choose an action word and watch Teddy act it out.

To help teddy get up the steps to his beloved honey, you must correctly count the numbers of everyday objects such as teddies, trees and clouds on a screen. The Letters game takes place at the fair - matching the letters displayed will earn your Teddy an ice cream. Parents may wish to offer the same reward to their children, but should watch out for E numbers. The colouring module is less a game and more an experiment in design - choose the colours of each item to form a picture.

418552.overview:
Fun School 4: for the under 5s is an educational game part of the Fun School series with this version aimed at the under-fives. There are six games and activities that allow the child to spend the day with Teddy and each activity has varying skill levels. The six activities are:

Teddy's House: Teddy's house is being painted but the painters don't know which colours to use so the child decides which colour to use for various parts of the house. After the painting is completed the child then has to tell the computer what colour certain objects are before being told a colour and what object to paint.

Fun Train: Teddy is at the funfair in the park and the child has to decide if a picture matches the picture on the train as well as words matching pictures.

Teddy Paint: This activity allows the child to use a simple art package to draw pictures with.

Teddy's Book's: It is time for bed and Teddy is having a sleepover with his friends. Daddy Ted is reading them a book from a shelf over the bed. The child has to decide which book Daddy is reading from the gap in the books on the shelf.

Teddy's Karaoke: This activity allows the child to sing various nursery rhymes from a choice of songs. The child can hear the song with the words on the screen. A bouncing ball bounces in time on the words to help the child follow the song.

Addition: Teddy is at school and has to do additions from the blackboard. The child is presented with a number of objects and the child has to say how many. Other skill levels have the child adding the objects before the pictures are removed and just the sum appears.

418954.overview: This is probably the best Commanche Clone on the Amiga until now, unfortunately just a short game demo instead of a full release.

418985.overview: Fanwor is an action-adventure in the style of the game "The Legend of Zelda". It was ported from either the Atari ST version or from the Linux version by Thomas Huth and released to the public domain in 2012. Later versions with updates from Lorence Lombardo and Stefan Haubenthal would be released, each adding additional features or improvements.

419139.overview: A 3D, isometric Diablo style RPG, based on unreleased Digital Reality SoftworX PC version. It was scheduled for release on Amiga/PC in late 1998, but was abandoned by the developers in 1999 due to the excessive complexity/size of the game. Italian developers Insonnia Team, headed by the game's gfx coder Marco Farace, reportedly took over the project from Digital Reality SoftworX, but nothing further was heard about the game and it remains unreleased. Internet previews of FORTRESS OF FEAR appeared on: Amiga Nutta (June 97) and Amiga Flame.

420711.overview: A simple demo of a bloody fighting game being developed for the Amiga by Mauro Antonio Radice aka MARadice with soundtrack by Alex Ciarelli. The game is being created in both English and Italian. In it you play Frank Brush and you and your two knives take on the world.

420867.overview: Homebrew demo platformer created by Pacific Software in 1996. Avoid the various enemies, the robots and penguins that will take you down. Pick up all the stars and make your way to the exit transporter to move to the next level.

420876.overview: Released as a preview on Amiga Future 129, this game is a clone of the old game Fort Apocalypse for Atari and C64, in which you traverse an underground prison area, destroying enemies and liberating its prisoners.

421043.overview:
Well the myth or mystery if you choose is over for some of us. For many many years Future Combat pt.II was available to playbut this was not the case for pt.1, did it ever exist or was pt.II just named that way we thought as there has been no pictures or any video footage of it anywhere,...well now that's changed and this mystery is finally closed and another missing gap in Amiga history has been filled. Thanks to one of the programmers confirming the first game did exist, there were a couple of ADFs available but neither worked but thanks to Ross "The Boss" he was able to fix the issues and now finally the first game can be played and here it is in full.

The game is very difficult, ship isn't spry and weapon upgrades will keep you wishing for more. No bosses but at least it has an end screen, the music is fine especially the high score table but really improves on the sequel.

421163.overview: Fatal Noise (also known as Fighting Cancer) is a unfinished playable demo fighting game for the Amiga. It was developed by Digital Waves.

421198.overview: This is a 1:1 arcade port of the game FROGGER by KONAMI from 1981 for the Amiga 500. The game is written in 68k assembler, based on the original Z80 code.

421273.overview: A freeware shooter created with AmiBlitz in 2020 by Fabrizio Radica aka fabbroz.  It is an upcoming top scrolling shoot em up, in which you must destroy waves of enemies and end of level bosses.

421362.overview: Scheduled for release in 1991, the game was cancelled when the project ran overtime and bugs in the code still remained unresolved. One becomes three. Anyone who buys Ubisoft's "Light Quest" gets three games at once. Basically, it's once again about freeing a fantasy kingdom from the clutches of demonic forces. However, whether you take on the fight against the evil Zora and her hordes of monsters as a warrior, as a cute Heinzelmann or as a magician is up to you. Depending on which form you choose, Lightquest presents itself as a thoroughbred action game, a thinking-heavy adventure game.

422033.overview: A puzzle game written in Blitz Basic by Philip Holden and released as shareware in 1995.

422034.overview: A cute SEUCK game in which you play a fish on the bottom of the ocean shooting at enemy fish. The game was developed by Bode Software and released into the public Domain in 1990.

422047.overview: A text-based adventure game by Jim MacBrayne. You've been given a shopping list by your aunt. After a gust of wind snatches it from your hand, you give chase... and then unfortunately fall into a manhole with a missing cover. A short while later, you find yourself at the bottom of the shaft, with a sword and lantern nearby.

422058.overview: A SEUCK based shareware game created by Micro Acid Software and released in 1994. Hop into your plane and shoot various incoming baddies.

422071.overview: Two players try to snatch each other's gems away in this AMOS game by Chris Banks in 1990. Released with Mutant Zombie Psycho Pigs on Spielekiste # 077.  This is a two player game, a duel to grab your opponent's Gem and survive. Different squares have different effects. Each player controls a Squiggly. Players take turns to jump 1 square in either direction But hurry as if you run out of time your Squiggly will explode. You Aim is to capture your opponents GEM. Some blocks that you jump on have special effects. Choose to read the (I)nformtion at the beginning of the game for full instructions.

422072.overview: A freeware game made by Infinite Gain Software. It would spawn a graphically enhanced version and a sequel. In it, you need to eat as many fish as you can. You can only eat fish smaller than yourself. At the start you can eat only small crabs, everything else will just sap your strength. Boss level is a shark you must defeat by death by a thousand nibbles. Go for the tail, it is the least dangerous end. Six levels of fun!

422073.overview: A vertically scrolling space shooter created by Andrew Fereday of FEZ Productions using the SEUCK in 1993.

422083.overview:
Based on the game originally released for 8 bit machines in published in Ahoy! 1987/11 (Issue #47). This version was rewritten for the Amiga by Efren Manuel Gonzales Puente. 

It is raining heavily outside your house, and the object of this game is to catch the falling raindrops before they fall down through the roof - depicted by the yellow line - and into the basement below. Once raindrops reach the basement, it starts to fill up with water. When the bucket is nearly full, you need to go to the sink at the right of the roof to empty it. Once you have caught enough raindrops, you proceed to the next level but the water level in the basement remains the same. The game ends if the basement is completely flooded.

422320.overview: Text adventure game created with Hatrack 2 by Bortphee Computers and released as freeware in 1992. Can you recover the Four Symbols? Can you prove yourself innocent of witchcraft? Will you curse the day you encountered the black cat? Will you survive? Only time will tell as your wits are challenged to the utmost on this seemingly simple quest, but with a sting in its tail!

422344.overview: A martial arts fighting game for two players. This is a fighting game very similar in style to Street Fighter.

422425.overview: A freeware fantasy RPG game. Choose your character and go on an adventure! Created by Scypsoft in 1989.

422535.overview: A German football management game by Jo Seitz in 1990.

422563.overview: Fortuna 2000 is a one to four player game loosely based on the TV show Wheel of Fortune, created by TAIR Chorzów and released by Atares in 1993. The players take turns guessing letters to form a word or a saying. The game can be played with up to four human players. During their turn the players can spin the wheel, guess a consonant, buy a vowel or guess the password.

422588.overview: A shareware, Polish language Wheel of Fortune game for up to three players by Gabriel Kalinowski in 1993.

422589.overview:
Frutis is an action game with puzzle-solving elements, a mix of Robbo and Boulder Dash games. The player must collect all the fruits and access keys, avoiding enemies and traps, moving cases blocking the road or switching different mechanisms. Contact with hostile creature or bullet blaster ends with the immediate death.

The game features a level editor.

422739.overview: Fun at the Sea is all about aiming to opponent's battleship by correct arrangement of deck cannon. The player may move the cannon left or right and change the angle to determine shot distance. Sinking the ship requires several customs hits. The game is designed for two players competing on a single horizontally divided screen.

422809.overview:
In this tactical game the player controls either a state from the Central Powers or the Entente and their African colonies and tries to win World War I.

The game is played on a tactical map showing Europe. This map is divided into provinces, e.g. Berlin or Normandy. The player can use several display modes in which the map shows attributes of the provinces, e.g. terrain or economic power. The movements of soldiers are ease to perform, they have to be dragged to their destination with the mouse. The combat is calculated by the computer after each turn.

The game has a detailed online help which explains gameplay mechanics and offers historical background information. In the shareware version is one scenario included which starts in 1914. After paying the registration fee the player gets access to additional scenarios and more units.

422811.overview: The game combines elements of Galaxian and Phoenix. It was programmed by Dirk Conrad in 100% 68k assembler. The music was composed by his buddy Carsten Schacht.  We had three tracks for the music and one track for sound effects. The whole game fit on a 880 KB floppy disk. Blast the aliens, use your shields if they get too close. Avoid the falling asteroids and shrapnel that comes from some types of enemies.

422999.overview:
A shareware puzzle game, written in AMOS and put out in 1996 by Hervé Robin. During the presentation screen, click the mouse to access the game. a grid with coordinates appears and you are asked to press the left button. at the bottom right is indicated a response time (6 seconds).
Locate carefully where the flower appears (ex: (8) and place it with a mouse click in the correct location on the grid, memorize the first flower and the lasers make a second appear. Place the two flowers back on the grid...etc... 

Demo version:
The demo version includes a sequence of up to 5 flowers to memorize. the full version has a much higher sequence of flowers and will give you a hard time!

423017.overview: A shareware solitaire card game created by Errol Wallingford of Sydenham Software and released in 1990 on 17-Bit Software.

423024.overview: Toss pressies at the various flying and land based baddies before they can spoil Christmas by tearing your guts out all over Monster Island. Be careful, if you miss you may have to pick up your pressie as you only have the few that fell out of the sleigh with you. Hold out and rack up points and enjoy the festive tunes and falling snow.

423032.overview: An Arkanoid\Breakout style shareware game from Steve Williams and Jayhawk, released in 1992.  The full version had over 50 levels and a level editor.

423354.overview: A German language freeware soccer\football management simulation created by Dirk Schaper in 1996 with updates continuing until 1998, the final known version was v1.9.

423357.overview: BatteMan's contribution to the Nouvim 3000 interactive fiction jam of 2020, the rules limit the amount of words to from 501 to 3000 to make things interesting. You are at home, in your small student room of barely 12m2. After going to the cinema with your best friend (long live the reduced prices and the 3 euro screenings on Monday evenings), you don't want to sleep, like many evenings for some time now... You don't you also don't want to do IRC or ICQ this evening... And you no longer have anything to watch, whether in VHS or DivX, and you don't want to go to the VHS distributor located a few hundred meters from your home. And the latest MP3 you want to listen to is still downloading to your computer...

423360.overview: An F1 management game for up to three players created by Crystal Interactive in 1996.

423446.overview: Full House is a beautifully done video poker game for one from BBS De Seen in 1990.

423449.overview: The game is a kind of clone of the Tron game, in which we must try to make the best possible tour without colliding with the limits of the circuit and without going over your rolls. Made by M. M. of New Wave in 1990. Released on the Terry 7 compilation. . It's a "Tron" variant, so you have to draw a track across the screen that intersects and doesn't even line up with the walls which will kill you if you come into contact with them. To make things easier, there are a limited number of jumps available, and the time you have to complete the course with four people is also variable. Although it is made quite simply, the game offers After so much action it becomes strategic thanks to the precise joystick control needed.

423626.overview: A fruit\slot machine game  with 3 reels, multiple betting lines, hold and double! A playable demo\preview from Project A on December 08, 1994.

423633.overview: Finding the story offers the child several sequences of events. Each sequence involves three images, which he must manipulate in order to put them in the proper chronological order. Several levels and game play modes are offered in relation to the child's age and progress. This game was released in Europe, published by Carraz Editions in 1989.

423644.overview: Part of a threesome of text adventures by the veteran text adventure writer, John Wilson. this is the second game in the series, following From Out of a Dark Night Sky and preceeding The Second Night. This game was created for multiple different platforms aside from the Amiga, including the Amstrad CPC, Atari ST, C16\Plus4, C64/128, CP/M, MSX, MSX2 and the Spectrum computers.

423663.overview:
A fantasy management program for German Grand Prix racing.  At the start of this Formula One season Autosport magazine started running a Fantasy Grand Prix competition. FGP is a program which allows you to avoid at the tedious working out how many places your driver gained on his grid position and just how many points did Rubens Barrichello score by coming third. FGP has a simple command line and takes most of its input in the form of human-readable ascii files which can be created on any text editor. FGP comes with all the current driver/team data files required and can handle up to 50 different teams. Example files are also included for the files you have to create yourself.

As of the German Grand Prix, Autosport introduced Fantasy Grand Prix II. This involved a small change to the scoring for chassis and engines. Release 2.02a of FGP uses these updated rules and the new drivers/teams as detailed in recent issues of Autosport.

423711.overview:
A funny, 4 player, comic\action\trading\adventure by Automagick Industries and released by Unicorn. The first release was in 1991 but had updates that continued through to version 2.91 in 1994. Versions were released in both English and German and demo versions as well as the full version from Unicorn.  
 
It is the year 1850 and you just got off the ship from the Old World in New York City. Your goal is simple: Become a famous hero. To put it in despicable numbers, this means one million Tier Points - whether we are embarked on a legal or illegal career, buy gold or hunt bears, indulge in a player career or rather fight for law as a deputy, is murmur, glory has many sides.

Before the Peacemaker is drawn for the first time, one to four Gunslingers can create their desired character by distributing 99 points on qualities such as wealth, reaction or drinking strength. The necessary (professional) utensils are then available in the New York shop, whereby care must be taken care that you always have a lot of viddles and water with you, because food is not available everywhere. Also, enough coal for the journey must remain inland, and anyone who values discussions with dignitaries (in the multiple choice procedure) is better concerned with new clothes, occasionally takes a bath and should be able to tolerate a sip of the hard stuff on the tongue.

Many actions end in small action scenes or tests. Anyone who wants to become an assistant sheriff must prove their shooting skills for bottles, cans and coins; bank robbers should prepare for a duel with the law enforcement officer. Fur hunters have to install their traps on a map and later find them without help. All these activities (and many more) then entrusted status points. Anyone who thinks that this is simple will be surprised: Even sheer survival is hard enough not to talk about becoming famous.

423713.overview: The topic is here the gods although Aztecan. The little god Athrijunk is thrown out of the world of gods by his bad uncle, therewith Athrijunk can not disturb his plans. The bad god plans to covertly kill the father of Athrijunk in the next booze. But the bad uncle hasn't unfortunately calculate that although gods in their own dimension are mortal - Athrijunk becomes immortal on the earth. Accordingly to that - it doesn't wondering us that the son of gods survives the bounce and now he is searching for a way back to his home. Fortunately he has his favorite toy - a bag with rainbowcrystals - he can produce stones of all color facets with that. If he managed it to produce a mosaic of an eagle with this stones und give him life - he has the chance to help his father. Colorful comic graphic, many music pieces and optical and acoustical effects are the features of this action thinking game.

423745.overview:
Intended to be a fully AGA supported version of the original Amiga Final Fight, work begun by "Paul Allen" but never completed. The streets of Metro City are filled with criminals who are part of a gang called Mad Gear. Former wrestler and newly elected mayor Mike Haggar tries to do something about it, much to the displeasure of the Mad Gear Gang who kidnap his daughter Jessica. Only three people are brave enough to venture into the crime-infested streets and try to bring Jessica back.

Final Fight is a 2D side-scrolling fighting game. Taking on the role of either Cody, Guy, or the mayor Mike Haggar himself, you must advance through six areas of the city clearing out the gang infestation. You will have to cope with a variety of thugs, ranging from firebomb-throwing maniacs to behemoth wrestlers. To defeat these thugs, you have an arsenal of punches, kicks, throws, and jump kicks at your disposal.

423835.overview:
The Polish language "Physics Tutor" program is helpful in mastering complex sections of natural sciences and contains 1000 questions (on one floppy disk) from all areas of physics. The topics cover the scope of primary and secondary schools. After initiating the program, a menu appears on the screen from which we can choose one of 25 sections of physics. Here is the full list:
Dynamics of a material point. Gravitational field
Phenomena of energy of state of aggregation of bodies. 
Electric pools in vacuum
Electric current
Electromagnetic induction
Electric oscillating circuits
Magnetic and other radiation
Solid state physics
Fluids and fluid dynamics
Constant number
Electrochemistry
Kinematics of a material point
Advanced Thermodynamics
1st law of thermodynamics Electrostatic field in insulators
A magnetic field
Vibrations and mechanical waves Emission and absorption in the shroud radius
Kinematics and dynamics of a rigid body
Nuclear physics
Acoustics
Waves Current in gases
After making your selection, the screen you will be on appears. The upper part of the screen is reserved for the content of the questions asked, the four squares in the middle of the screen contain the answers (one of them is true, and on the right side of the screen there are two figures indicating the number of correct and incorrect answers). At any time during the test, we can turn on or turn off a rather pleasant patch accompanying our struggles. The questions asked during the tests are quite diverse. Some are quasi theoretical, others require you to do some calculations on a piece of paper, there are also those in which the answer is to point to the appropriate drawing or chart. If we answer the question correctly, an inscription will appear indicating success.

424701.overview: A Swedish-language, children's educational painting game for one person, created by  Mikael Svanholm and Andreas Lindholm and published by SPAB in 1991. Color the words as you learn them!

440401.overview:
This was a one-person hobby project which took just under three years to complete.

It was also the first time programming the Amiga, so much of the  development period was spent learning how to code from scratch in 68000 assembly language, as well as navigating the Amiga's custom hardware.

The game is not a remake of the 1991 creative materials release, but rather a new version for ecs 2mb Amigas, with the "enhanced" in Final Fight: Enhanced referring to the "enhanced chip set".

-New Music
-Additional characters
-Vastly improved gameplay

440418.overview: Came in tenth place in the RetroKomp 2016 GameDev Compo in Poland. But you might see red that you don't see those famous Testarossa colors on screen in this simple line graphics game by Sordan. In actuality, this is a very simple freeware AMOS racing game, with black and white graphics, that said the digitized sounds are pretty good. you get points for every car you pass, see if you can beat the author's best score of 117.

442412.overview: This a flappy bird clone made for the Amiga 500 computer. It should also work for all Amigas versions (but hasn't been tested) since it's using relatively primitive and basic graphics and isn't interacting much with the OS.

443941.overview: Tetris with Jewels instead of tetrominos. Each level gives you a goal to reach in order to complete it. Complete a number of vertical columns of matching jewels or a number or horizontal or diagonal ones. You can see the next four jewels that will come into play. Created by Jonathan Lepper and Chinatown with music by Slim. Published by Soft and Easy in 1992

446006.overview: Koło Fortuny is a simple video game loosely based on the TV game show of the same name, Wheel of Fortune in the US. The players take turns guessing letters to form a word or a saying. It can be played with up to two human players. The game takes 5 rounds all together. Each vowel costs 200 points. There are no graphics (like wheel spin) in the game, all is presented in text mode.

446335.overview: A sequel to Trapped 2, based on a revised and corrected version of the Trapped 2 engine. This new marvel will be called Fratzen Geballer and will implement new and spectacular effects such as mipmapping. lensflares, dithering and very atmospheric lighting effects. Everything will be set in a space station. The game would remain unreleased, with this demo dropped in 1997.

447292.overview: This a 2D, 2 players racing game demo I coded in blitz basic 2 when I was fifteen and I was the only person coding and having an amiga in my countryside. So please no jugement, I cry myself when I read the code 26 years later.

448153.overview:
The second in the game series that helps those who speak German to learn to speak French. Grammar: in 12 or 11 interactive chapters, all important grammar areas are explained in detail and with many examples. Practice included with around 1000 integrated grammar tasks.  7 vocabulary trainers with the entire basic vocabulary (approx. 2300 words and 1200 idioms), editor for your own libraries, learning in context, and much more. Verb trainer & verb tables (French II only): irregular verbs can be displayed as verb tables in the course and learned completely flexibly in the trainer. Precise correction function for all keyboard entries. Online dictionary and technical terminology are available at any time. 
Independent of textbooks - therefore suitable for adults as well as students. Update service for registered customers.

448162.overview: An editor for Football League games to allow you to update stats or fix issues, make your dream teams and play them together to find out who really would be best. Play Pelé, Diego Maradona, and Lionel Messi against Cristiano Ronaldo, Johan Cruyff, and Franz Beckenbauer for a dream team game. The options are endless.

449067.overview:
The computer managing the space base has malfunctioned and you must find a way to disable it. To complete your mission, you'll need to piece together a message by discovering the missing words one by one. You'll have to explore a complex maze with numerous elevators to move from one level to the next, and it's very easy to get lost.

Along the way, you'll find extra ammunition and, most importantly, access cards to certain computers. Once connected to the corresponding computer (which you must first discover), you'll still need to find the access code to learn one of the words in the message. The numerous robot guards and laser turrets won't make your task any easier. Fortunately, they won't be able to withstand your fire for long.

449070.overview:
An AMOS based shareware adventure game from Satchel Software in 1991. Flowers of Crystal is an educational game from the author of Granny's Garden. The game was designed to provide for creative activities in the classroom and is built around puzzle-solving. It consists of three parts: an introductory story and an adventure in two parts. A password from the first part is required to start the second. The introductory story is also included recorded on an audio tape as well as printed in a booklet.

The game takes place on the planet Crystal which once had vast expanses of colorful flowers that are now thought to be extinct. The player is a visitor from Earth who explores the planet in an attempt to find the last remaining flower. In the first part, the player has to find four objects (special water, gold pot, fertilizer and soil). The game play involves traveling between seven locations (center, city, factory, forest, lake, desert and mountains) and choosing which items to carry. The game starts out at the center where the player chooses four items from three different menus. Items are needed when visiting some of the locations or give some protection when encountering hazards or some of the world's hostile creatures. The second part involves finding six parts of a flower dream to recreate a complete flower picture and then go to a castle. To progress it is necessary to obtain spells and use them at the right location. 
 
 Game was distributed in a clear plastic satchel with disks and other items packed inside the manual. Hence the manual covers also serve as a "box cover"

449071.overview:
A commercial flight simulator release from Matt Shaw, Ted Jump and Hill Manders of Jaeger Software in 1993. One of many releases in this series. It supported oene or two players and vs play. It was released as both a standalone product and as a data disk to be used together with the original release of FIGHTER DUEL PRO. Like the original, you fly combat air patrols (CAP) in WW2 aircraft armed with guns only, in three separate areas located around your carrier base, against 1-2 computer opponents, or against a single human opponent. An analog rudder control has been added (you can still use the mouse), and also an optional rear view, using a second Amiga and monitor connected with a special parallel cable.

Scorekeeping and tournament modes have also been added, and there is a simple replay mode, in which you can review the last minute of your flight, from your own viewpoint only. There is a 'turbo' panning function to move around the map quicker, which also has updated scenery. You can play single-player against 1-2 computer controlled pilots, or two human players using modem or null-modem connection, with many WW2 aircraft to choose from.  
 
The added bonus of this version was the ability to create realistic, complex motion paths for use with LightWave 3D. Can also generate FDPro demo reels to review flights. Create in minutes an aerodynamically correct flight path that once took years, or a company's logo move that took weeks. Simultaneously records position and attitude information for three aircraft at 30 frames/sec for 45 mins on 9MB system. Motionpaths are then imported into LightWave 3D to animate flying objects, camera viewpoint, aircraft, logos. Control 2nd and 3rd aircraft by computer or via serial port link.

449094.overview: Fortuna (or Kolo Fortuny) was an AMOS based Polish language commercial release from Twin Spark Soft in 1993. This is a Wheel of Fortune style game in Polish where you would try to solve the puzzle while dealing with the randomness of the what the wheel gave in terms of points per correct guess, while avoiding the bankrupts.

449096.overview: Learn French (for English speakers) with French Grammar 1, created with AmigaBasic by Intellectual Software and published by Queue in 1988. 10 modules to help you review French Grammar, including 2 modules on gender of nouns, gender and number, plural of nouns, nouns and articles, definite articles, prepositions, avoir and etre, idioms with avoir and il est and c'est. When you finish this you can move on to French Grammar 2 and 3, published the same year.

449402.overview: Flip Over is a Freeware 1993 game made with AMOS by Mantisoft (Killian Breslin). Flip-Over: Small mouse-controlled thinking and strategy game from the green bell class. Must be on a 3x3 to 8x8 field Stones can be recolored by clicking on them. Since each then the surrounding fields are exposed to the sudden color change, are partial successes achieved with difficulty get there quickly. (Similarities to the Rubik's Cube are not to be dismissed out of hand.)

449591.overview:
"Foundation: The Undiscovered Land" refers to an expansion pack for the real-time strategy game "Foundation," adding new gameplay elements and missions that involve exploring and developing uncharted territories within the game world, essentially introducing a new area to build and manage beyond the initial map boundaries. 
Key points about "Foundation: The Undiscovered Land":

    Expansion pack:
    It is not a standalone game, but an add-on that requires the base "Foundation" game to play.
    New map areas:

461892.overview:
FastLife, or the Game of Life

The Game of Life was invented by Cambridge University mathematician John Horton Conway in 1968. The game is based on a cellular automaton and is played on a two-dimensional grid. Readers wishing to explore the subject further can consult the article by A.K. Dewdney in *Le Scienze* No. 224 (April 1987), titled "Computer Recreations." There are only two rules in this game: the rules of Birth and Death.

Birth: A cell is born in any square that has exactly three living neighbors.

Death: A cell dies of isolation if it has fewer than two living neighbors, and dies of overcrowding if it has more than three living neighbors.

Neighbors include those located diagonally, horizontally, and vertically; thus, each square has eight potential neighbor positions. As the game progresses through successive generations, cells are born and die according to these rules. Newly born cells can only cause other cells to be born or die in the generation following their own birth. As you experiment with different starting patterns, a number of recurring, stable shapes will become familiar to you. Figure out how to keep it alive the longest!

482092.overview:
Forbidden Forest on Amiga: Paul Norman's 8-bit Horror Masterpiece, Purist and Remastered

Some games are remembered for their gameplay. Forbidden Forest (Cosmi, 1983) is remembered for how it made you feel.

On a humble Commodore 64, Paul Norman built something nobody had seen before: a forest that breathes, a sky that moves from day to dusk to a starry night, parallax backgrounds, giant spiders, bees, frogs, dragons, a snake, skeletons rising from the ground, and finally the Demogorgon, unseen in the darkness until the lightning reveals it. It was cinematic, violent and genuinely frightening, years before anyone spoke of "survival horror".

This project brings that masterpiece to the Amiga in three editions: two purist ones, faithful to the last pixel, and a remake that reimagines its world with new graphics while keeping its soul intact.
